top_categories.workout_context: 313 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 313 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 313 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
At Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
313 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship's mixed terrain actually does to you.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship. Train it until it feels boring.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 313 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Manali-Khardung La Cycling Championship demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride mixed terrain at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Test tires and pressure in comparable conditions before race week rather than guessing from a generic time-loss claim.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 313 miles of mixed terrain in Manali to Leh, Himachal Pradesh / Ladakh, India.
